claim.quote: Here the CMS Collaboration reports the most up-to-date combination of results on the properties of the Higgs boson, including the most stringent limit on the cross section for the production of a pair of Higgs bosons, on the basis of data from proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV.

date.note: arXiv submission date; published as Nature 607 (2022) 60

name: A portrait of the Higgs boson ten years after the discovery

significance.note: A combination paper reporting many measurements; no single significance is quoted in the abstract.

summary.plain: Ten years after the discovery, CMS reported what it calls the most up-to-date combination of its results on the Higgs boson's properties (decays, spin-parity, mass and production), together with a limit on Higgs boson pair production. The collaboration says that, within the uncertainties, all these observations are compatible with the Standard Model.
summary.technical: Combination of CMS 13 TeV results on the Higgs boson: observed in numerous fermionic and bosonic decay channels, spin-parity quantum numbers established, mass determined and production cross sections measured in various modes, including what the collaboration calls 'the most stringent limit on the cross section for the production of a pair of Higgs bosons'; within the uncertainties all observations are compatible with the standard model.

title: A portrait of the Higgs boson by the CMS experiment ten years after the discovery
why_it_matters: The abstract says much evidence points to the standard model being a low-energy approximation of a more comprehensive theory, that several of the standard model issues originate in the Higgs boson sector, and that the order-of-magnitude larger number of Higgs bosons expected to be examined over the next fifteen years will help deepen understanding of this sector.
